newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PAKISTAN STOCKS OFFER BARGAINS - SOCGEN CROSBY.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN STOCKS OFFER BARGAINS - SOCGEN CROSBY.

text.p: Pakistani stocks offer some of the best bargains in the region, according to an analysis by SocGen-Crosby Securities released on Friday.
"Pakistan is one of the cheapest markets from a regional perspective with three-year forward earnings growth at 23 percent and trading at (a multiple of) 6.7X," it said.
The Karachi 100-index rose 13.84 points, or 0.69 percent, to 2,027.05 on Friday. It now stands 27.25 percent higher than its level of 1,592.86 points on July 1, the start of fiscal 1997/98.

SocGen-Crosby attributed the recent rise to political stability, upward re-rating of fundamentals, excess liquidity, anticipation of reaching a new loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund and re-rating of forward earnings.
"Although corporate earnings growth forecasts remain unchanged, the above factors have led to an upward re-rating of the market multiple," the report said.
"The lower risk perception of the Pakistani economy, coupled with the more stable political outlook and increased liquidity flows, has raised the floor of the index.

"After hovering between 7.5X and 8X one-year forward earnings for the last year, the multiple has now re-rated with a base of 1,850-1,875 points, putting the floor of the index at around 9X one-year forward earnings," it said.
SocGen-Crosby said these factors could provide the catalyst for local retail buying, but added that risks remained.
Pakistan's prospects for reviving its economy, still highly dependent on agricultural produce, hinged on achieving a cotton crop in excess of 10 million 375-lb bales, it said.

"Combined with our strong valuations, we recommend stocks like Engro Chemical, Muslim Commercial Bank, Askari Bank, Lever Bros, Packages Ltd, Sui Northern Gas and Adamjee Insurance, which have the best potential for out-performance in the short term," SocGen-Crosby said.
The market capitalisation of the 782 companies listed at the Karachi Stock Exchange rose to 605.276 billion rupees in July from 491.880 billion in June, KSE figures show.
